name: Pennsylvania

creditorClaims.text: Pennsylvania has no short non-claim bar date: death does not stop limitation periods, but a claim that would expire within 1 year after death is extended to 1 year after death (20 Pa.C.S. § 3383); written notice of a claim to the personal representative tolls limitations (§ 3384); claims become unenforceable after 1 year from death against bona fide purchasers of the decedent's real estate in the cases of § 3385. The one-year protection for distribution after advertisement of letters (§ 3532) could not be read.

earliestClose.text: Not verified: the rule protecting a personal representative who distributes more than 1 year after first advertisement of letters (20 Pa.C.S. § 3532) could not be read from an official source.

smallEstate.text: Settlement of small estates on petition to the orphans' court division when the decedent's property (excluding real estate and payments under § 3101, including the family exemption) has a gross value not exceeding $50,000 (20 Pa.C.S. § 3102, as amended by Act 35 of July 2, 2013, effective 60 days later, for decedents dying on or after that date). Not indexed.

simplified.text: Small estate petition for estates up to $50,000 (20 Pa.C.S. § 3102); payments to family and funeral directors of certain wages, deposits and benefits without administration (20 Pa.C.S. § 3101).

filingFee.text: Philadelphia Register of Wills probate fees depend on estate value (base fee + 20% tax + $176.25 filing fees, schedule effective September 26, 2022, published 11/18/2024): total $190.25 for $0-$250; $386.25 for $10,000.01-$50,000; $491.25 for $50,000.01-$200,000; $596.25 for $200,000.01-$300,000; rising by $105 per $100,000 bracket to $1,331.25 for the first $1,000,000; plus $75 base ($15 tax) per additional $100,000 and $750 base ($150 tax) per additional $1,000,000.

personalRepFee.text: No statutory percentage schedule in Title 20; personal representative compensation is allowed by the orphans' court as reasonable (20 Pa.C.S. § 3537, not read).

attorneyFee.text: No statutory schedule; attorney fees are allowed by the orphans' court as reasonable (20 Pa.C.S. § 3537, not read).
